stories.title: Netflix Buys Historic Radford Studio Center in L.A. for $380M
stories.excerpt: Netflix has acquired one of Los Angeles’ landmark film and television studios at a steep discount, as the region’s struggling entertainment industry continues to weigh on production real estate. The streaming giant announced Tuesday that it is purchasing the 55-acre, 1.2 million-square-foot Radford Studio Center in Studio City for $380 million from Goldman Sachs. The price is a 79 percent discount from the $1.85 billion that Hackman Capital Partners and its investors paid for the property in 2021. The acquisition follows Hackman’s default on a $1.1 billion mortgage, which led to Goldman Sachs taking control of the property. The studio received no bids at a foreclosure auction Tuesday morning, approximately an hour before Netflix announced the deal, according to Bloomberg. Netflix expects the deal to close Tuesday evening. The company plans to keep Radford operating as a working production studio, with existing productions continuing uninterrupted. Opened in 1928, Radford has hosted television classics including “Seinfeld,” “Gunsmoke,” “Gilligan’s Island” and “The Mary Tyler Moore Show.” The acquisition comes as Southern California’s production downturn continues to pressure studio owners. Hackman has faced distress across several properties, including Television City, the 25-acre Fairfax District studio where lenders led by Deutsche Bank moved toward foreclosure earlier this year. The company also faced pressure involving Manhattan Beach Studios, while Fortress Investment Group foreclosed on its Sony Animation campus in Culver City. Los Angeles-area film and television employment declined 36 percent from 2022 through 2025, according to the Los Angeles County Department of Economic Opportunity. Production shoot days fell nearly 5 percent annually in the most recent quarter, according to FilmLA. bullets: Netflix acquires Radford Studio Center, L.A., 55 acres for $380M (79% discount from 2021)
Hackman Capital defaulted on $1.1B mortgage; Goldman Sachs foreclosed; zero auction bids
Studio remains operational production facility; signals L.A. entertainment real estate distress
stories.summary: Netflix purchased the 1.2M-sf Radford Studio Center in Studio City for $380M from Goldman Sachs, a 79% markdown from the $1.85B Hackman Capital paid in 2021. Hackman defaulted on a $1.1B mortgage, triggering foreclosure with zero bids at auction. Netflix will maintain the site as an active production studio. The steep discount reflects the struggling L.A. entertainment production sector.
stories.impact: Los Angeles production real estate distress indicates softening demand for specialized office/industrial facilities tied to entertainment; collateral damage from streaming consolidation and production slowdown reduces competing land use intensity in L.A. submarkets, potentially freeing parcels for mixed-use or residential redevelopment. Signals capital losses for finance players and suggests cap rate expansion in media-dependent property classes, raising underwriting caution for similar-use assets.

stories.title: Law Firms Expand Office Footprints as Leasing Nears Annual Record
stories.excerpt: U.S. law firms are on pace for a second straight record year of office leasing, with many still looking to expand their real estate footprints. The legal sector leased nearly 5 million square feet of office space in the third quarter of 2026, up 23 percent from the same period last year and the strongest third quarter on record, according to a report released Tuesday by Cushman & Wakefield. Law firms have collectively leased 17.5 million square feet through the first nine months of 2026, up 21 percent compared to 2025, and just 1.4 million square feet shy of the annual record set last year. “Law firm demand has not only held its pace, it has accelerated,” David C. Smith, Cushman & Wakefield’s head of Americas insights, said in a statement. “Every quarter of 2026 has outpaced its 2025 counterpart, and with one quarter remaining, the sector is positioned to surpass last year’s record total. “What stands out is that this growth is coming from firms expanding their footprints, not simply maintaining their size,” Smith added. The country’s 10 largest legal office markets accounted for 3.1 million square feet of leasing in the third quarter, and 11.2 million square feet of activity so far this year. The annual figure is just 100,000 square feet below the markets’ combined annual record set last year. New York City led all markets with 1.1 million square feet of leasing by legal firms in the third quarter. Atlanta was No. 2 with 454,000 square feet, marking its strongest quarter for legal sector leasing since 2017. Washington, D.C., accounted for 8 percent of third-quarter leasing nationwide, followed by Los Angeles at 6 percent, and Boston and San Francisco at 4 percent each. Meanwhile, Chicago and New York City have each already surpassed their 2025 law firm leasing totals. Demand also extended well beyond the country’s traditional legal hubs. Markets outside the top 10 accounted for 1.9 million square feet, or 38 percent of third-quarter leasing activity. Seven
bullets: Law firms leased 17.5M sf through Q3 2026, up 21% YoY; on track to exceed 2025 record

stories.summary: U.S. law firms leased 17.5M square feet through the first nine months of 2026, up 21% from 2025, tracking to surpass last year's annual record. Q3 2026 alone saw nearly 5M sf leased, up 23% year-over-year and the strongest third quarter on record. Growth is fueled by firms expanding footprints rather than simply maintaining existing space, according to Cushman & Wakefield.
stories.impact: Accelerating legal sector office demand signals sustained high-end employment growth and professional services confidence across major metros (NYC, DC, L.A. hubs likely leading); strong tenant demand supports office valuations and reduces cap-rate pressure in Class A markets, improving financing conditions for mixed-use and office-to-residential conversion projects. This employment resilience supports adjacent multifamily demand in downtown submarkets where law firms cluster.

stories.title: Hudson River Trading Expands to 551K SF at 3 World Trade Center
stories.excerpt: Hudson River Trading (HRT), a leading electronic and quantitative trading firm, has added a large chunk of office space to its global headquarters at 3 World Trade Center. HRT, which moved into its Financial District home in 2018, just signed a lease to add 340,000 square feet to its existing 211,207-square-foot office at 175 Greenwich Street, according to landlord Silverstein Properties. The new expansion brings HRT’s total footprint at 3 World Trade Center to approximately 551,207 square feet. The 15-year expansion lease had an asking rent between $110 and $150 per square foot, according to a source familiar with the deal. Before moving into 3 World Trade Center, HRT leased 70,000 square feet at 4 World Trade Center starting in 2016. Its relocation to 3 World Trade Center in 2018 gave it 136,000 square feet of office space, and HRT later added another 75,207 square feet to its footprint in 2021. The trading firm’s latest expansion deal brings the 80-story 3 World Trade Center to 98 percent occupancy, according to Silverstein. “Hudson River Trading is home to some of the most creative and brilliant people in New York, and its extraordinary growth at the World Trade Center is a testament to the appeal of this location,” Jeremy Moss, executive vice president at Silverstein, said in a statement. “Today’s announcement reflects the company’s confidence in Lower Manhattan and the advantages of working in a modern, highly connected building that can grow with its tenants.” A spokesperson for HRT added that the expansion represents “an investment in our people and in our future.” Moss represented Silverstein in-house in the deal, alongside a CBRE team of Mary Ann Tighe, Ken Meyerson, Evan Haskell and Caroline Merck. Sacha Zarba, Chris Corrinet and Jeff Fischer, also from CBRE, brokered the deal for HRT. A spokesperson for CBRE did not immediately respond to a request for comment. stories.summary: Hudson River Trading signed a 15-year lease for 340,000 additional square feet at 3 World Trade Center, expanding its total footprint to 551,207 sf. The expansion lease carried asking rents between $110–$150/sf. The deal brings the 80-story building to 98% occupancy and marks HRT's third major expansion since relocating to the site in 2018.
stories.impact: Financial District office strength (98% occupancy at 3 WTC, major quant-trading tenant locking in long lease) validates NYC Financial District recovery and signals stable institutional employment demand; full occupancy reduces cap-rate upside but underscores security for mixed-use residential projects in lower Manhattan, supporting underwriting of office-to-multifamily conversions and new mixed-use development around transit hubs.

stories.title: Irvine Retail Center Sells for $31.4M
stories.excerpt: Trade Marketplace, a 32,560-square-foot retail center in Irvine, sold for a reported $31.4 million ($964/sf). The property, located at 2222 and 2272 Michelson Drive, was acquired by an undisclosed private investor. Situated on just over three acres, Trade Marketplace comprises two buildings featuring a mix of traditional retail suites and an indoor-outdoor food hall. Originally built in 1989, the property was repositioned in 2017. Tenants include HiroNori Craft Ramen, Financial Partners Credit Union, Domino’s Pizza and Subway, along with a collection of independent dining and service businesses. The center is located within the Irvine Business Complex, near John Wayne Airport and Interstate 405. The surrounding one-mile radius contains approximately 18.4 million square feet of office space and 11,500 multifamily units. Christopher Smith and Andrey Mindirgasov with Colliers represented the buyer in the transaction. The seller, Dream Square Irvine LLC, an entity managed by Japan-based Daiwa House Group, acquired the property in 2019 for $30.75 million. The asset was previously marketed for sale in 2023. bullets: Trade Marketplace, Irvine, sold for $31.4M ($964/sf); 32,560 sf retail center

stories.summary: Trade Marketplace, a 32,560-sf retail center in Irvine comprising two buildings with traditional retail and an indoor-outdoor food hall, sold for $31.4M ($964/sf) to an undisclosed private investor. The seller, Daiwa House-managed Dream Square Irvine LLC, acquired it in 2019 for $30.75M. The property sits within the Irvine Business Complex, surrounded by 18.4M sf of office and 11,500 multifamily units.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Static pricing ($30.75M→$31.4M over seven years) reflects mature Irvine retail underperformance; however, high office and MF density nearby (18.4M sf office, 11,500 units) confirms Irvine Business Complex as anchored employment/residential hub. Retail stagnation does not threaten multifamily demand in this submarket; food-hall positioning may signal defensive retail-to-dining repositioning rather than growth.

stories.title: Golden State Orthopedics & Spine Signs Lease for 15,000 SF in San Ramon
stories.excerpt: Golden State Orthopedics & Spine (GSOS) has inked a 15,000-square-foot lease at Bishop Ranch in San Ramon for a new orthopedic clinic and physical therapy facility. The practice expects to open the location in early 2027. The space is located at 2633 Camino Ramon, a five-story, 242,000-square-foot LEED Gold-certified building. The structure is part of Sycamore at Bishop Ranch, a four-building, 935,000-square-foot office campus owned by Sunset Development Company. Situated less than a mile from San Ramon Regional Medical Center, the new facility will support the practice’s continued expansion throughout Northern California while addressing growing demand for orthopedic services in the Tri-Valley region. Financial terms of the transaction were not disclosed, however, we understand that space at the property is being marketed at an asking rate of $3.35 per square foot per month, full-service gross. Justin Grilli and Mike Zylstra with Newmark represented GSOS in the transaction. CBRE handles leasing responsibilities for the office campus. Newmark has advised GSOS on several expansion initiatives over the past 18 months. The post Golden State Orthopedics & Spine Signs Lease for 15,000 SF in San Ramon appeared first on Connect CRE.

stories.summary: Golden State Orthopedics & Spine signed a 15,000-sf lease at Bishop Ranch in San Ramon for a new orthopedic clinic and physical therapy facility opening in early 2027. The space is at 2633 Camino Ramon within the four-building, 935,000-sf Sycamore at Bishop Ranch campus, leased at $3.35/sf/month. Proximity to San Ramon Regional Medical Center supports the practice's Northern California expansion.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance. Tri-Valley healthcare facility expansion signals growing senior/medical demand in the region, which supports multifamily demand for age-55+ and workforce housing near medical centers; however, this is an office/medical lease, not a residential signal. It reinforces Bishop Ranch/San Ramon as a stable employment hub and suggests continued residential demand from healthcare workers and older adults relocating toward medical services.

stories.title: Orange County Department of Education Starts Work on $21M Environmental Education Development
stories.excerpt: The Orange County Department of Education has broken ground on Rancho Soñado Inside the Outdoors Education Center in Silverado, a $21-million, multi-building campus in eastern Orange County. C.W. Driver Companies is the general contractor for the project, which will restore a longtime environmental education campus largely destroyed by the 2020 Bond Fire. Located at 8755 Santiago Canyon Rd., the 110-acre property will feature 19,885 square feet of new facilities designed to provide hands-on environmental education for students from pre-kindergarten through high school. The development includes a 3,637-square-foot multipurpose environmental education building, a 4,382-square-foot covered outdoor instructional area, four 823-square-foot educational pavilions, a 133-seat amphitheater, an administrative building and an outdoor dining pavilion. Designed to enhance wildfire resiliency, the campus will incorporate noncombustible construction materials, interior and exterior sprinkler systems and improved emergency vehicle access. Other improvements include expanded vehicle and bus parking, accessible learning spaces and native, drought-tolerant landscaping. The development team also includes tBP/Architecture, project manager Schoolhaus Advisors Inc. and landscape architect Conceptual Design + Planning Company. Construction is slated for completion in December 2027. stories.summary: The Orange County Department of Education broke ground on Rancho Soñado Inside the Outdoors Education Center in Silverado, a $21M multi-building campus on 110 acres designed to restore environmental education facilities destroyed by the 2020 Bond Fire. The project includes 19,885 sf of new structures with noncombustible construction, interior/exterior sprinkler systems and improved emergency access. C.W. Driver Companies is the general contractor.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. Public education capital investment in rural eastern Orange County signals ongoing recovery and regional stabilization post-wildfire; may modestly support workforce housing demand for educators and support staff in Silverado area, but does not alter regional supply/demand fundamentals for multifamily development.

stories.title: Santa Clara Apartment Trade Comes in at $360K per Unit
stories.excerpt: In a recent Bay Area apartment comp, a private investor paid $6.13 million for a 17-unit multifamily property in Santa Clara. The property, located at 165 Monroe Street, sold for $360,500 per unit. Built in 1960, the 12,775-square-foot property is situated on a 0.48-acre parcel and consists of all one- and two-bedroom units. Select units feature upgraded interiors with stainless steel appliances, quartz countertops, hardwood flooring and modern cabinetry. Community amenities include an on-site laundry facility, swimming pool and private tuck-under parking. The property is within walking distance of Santa Clara University and near Westfield Valley Fair and Santana Row, providing residents with access to shopping, dining and entertainment.  Rob Johnston, Adam Levin and Noah Lee of the Levin Johnston team in Marcus & Millichap’s Palo Alto office represented the buyer and procured the seller, also a private investor. “The buyer plans to continue the interior renovations already completed in approximately half of the units,” commented Johnston. “The South Bay rental market remains strong, with continued interest from investors seeking multifamily opportunities in the area.” The post Santa Clara Apartment Trade Comes in at $360K per Unit appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Santa Clara apartment trade: $6.13M for 17-unit property; $360.5K per unit

stories.summary: A private investor purchased a 17-unit multifamily property at 165 Monroe Street in Santa Clara for $6.13M ($360,500/unit). The 1960-built, 12,775-sf property sits on 0.48 acres with one- and two-bedroom units, amenities include pool and tuck-under parking. The buyer plans to continue interior renovations. Marcus & Millichap cited continued South Bay investor interest in multifamily.
stories.impact: South Bay apartment valuations holding at $360.5K/unit signals stable rental demand near Santa Clara University and Westfield Valley Fair; transaction confirms sustained investor appetite for value-add multifamily in the Bay Area despite broader regional affordability stress. Market stability supports development feasibility in Santa Clara and adjacent Silicon Valley submarkets, though per-unit pricing and density constraints remain tight for new-build economics.

stories.title: Miami Investor Buys Fort Lauderdale Retail Center for $35M
stories.excerpt: Core Investment Management has paid $35.4 million for a strip mall in Fort Lauderdale, following a four-year repositioning. The 73,756-square-foot asset called Gateway Shopping District features 11 buildings between 1914 and 1980 East Sunrise Boulevard. The strip mall is sandwiched between 18th Northeast Avenue and 20th Northeast Avenue, near the 799,851-square-foot Galleria Mall, which is slated to be redeveloped into a mixed-use development. Gateway Shopping District is just under 90 percent leased, according to a representative for Native Realty, which brokered the sale, though Adam Greenberg, a managing partner at Core, put the figure closer to the low 80s. Tenants include Peppi’s Pizza, Stretch Zone, Barolo and Pulp & Press. The sale excluded the corner building at 1990 East Sunrise Boulevard. The Miami-based buyer took out a $20 million loan from International Finance Bank. First developed as a quarry and later as a jungle zoo in 1940, the property was gradually turned into a shopping center starting in the 1950s. In recent years, the center had fallen into disrepair, and in 2022, Native CEO Jaime Sturgis was hired by the separate owners of the retail buildings to rehab and lease up the asset. “Our job was to listen, build trust and find a path that worked for everyone,” Sturgis said in a statement. “Seeing this property transform from a neglected shopping center into one of the most dynamic retail destinations in Fort Lauderdale, and then closing a sale of this size, is incredibly rewarding.” Core, which also counts Michael Lapointe as a managing partner, specializes in retail, specifically strip malls and grocery-anchored properties, across Florida. Last year, the investor purchased a Publix-anchored shopping center in Plantation, Fla., for $53 million. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Core Investment Management acquires Gateway Shopping District, Fort Lauderdale, for $35.4M

stories.summary: Core Investment Management purchased Gateway Shopping District, a 73,756-sf strip mall in Fort Lauderdale comprising 11 buildings, for $35.4M following a four-year repositioning. The property is 80–90% leased with tenants including Peppi's Pizza, Stretch Zone and Barolo. The buyer financed the deal with a $20M loan from International Finance Bank. The property sits near the 799,851-sf Galleria Mall, which is slated for redevelopment into mixed-use.
stories.impact: Retail repositioning success (four-year hold, strong occupancy) in Fort Lauderdale signals underlying residential and commercial demand in the submarket; however, proximity to Galleria mixed-use redevelopment indicates potential near-term competitive pressure on standalone retail. The Galleria conversion likely to introduce new residential, office and dining, fragmenting retail tenant pools. Developers should monitor Galleria timeline as a catalyst for retail-to-mixed-use conversion plays or ground-lease opportunities near that site.

stories.title: Nursing Home Operator Offloads Bronx, Queens Care Facilities for $178M
stories.excerpt: Two New York City nursing home facilities have found a new owner. Entities tied to health care operators and frequent partners Infinite Care and Emerald Group have secured a 448-bed facility in the Bronx and a 314-bed facility in Queens for a combined $177.5 million, according to city records filed Tuesday. The properties’ sellers are affiliated with senior care home operator Centers Health Care, co-owned by Kenneth Rozenberg and investor Daryl Hagler. In November 2024, Centers for Care and its affiliates arrived at a $45 million settlement with the New York Attorney General over alleged financial fraud and resident neglect at four facilities, including the two that just changed hands. The priciest of the two transactions took place at Beth Abraham Center for Rehabilitation and Nursing, located at 612 Allerton Avenue in the Bronx’s Allerton neighborhood. The seller, Light Property Holdings Associates, parted with the property for $89 million, according to the first filing. Hagler signed for the seller. Beth Abraham Center’s new owner, 612 Allerton SNF Realty, is linked to both Infinite Care and Emerald Group. The entity secured $78.7 million in financing for its purchase from Huntington National Bank. The second transaction filed Tuesday saw the Holliswood Center for Rehabilitation and Healthcare in Queens’ Hollis neighborhood trade for $88.5 million. The property is at 195-44 Sagamore Avenue. Hagler also signed for the seller, Hollis Real Estate. Infinite Care and Emerald Group, through 195-44 Woodhull SNF Realty, financed the purchase with another $66.4 million loan. It was not immediately clear whether the Centers Health Care affiliates will continue on at the two properties as tenants and operators. Representatives for Infinite Health, Emerald Group, Centers Health Care and Huntington National Bank did not immediately respond to requests for comment. Emily Davis can be reached at edavis@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Infinite Care & Emerald Group buy Centers Health Care nursing homes (Bronx, Queens) for $177.5M
Beth Abraham Center (Bronx), 448 beds, $89M; Queens facility, 314 beds, $88.5M

stories.summary: Entities tied to Infinite Care and Emerald Group acquired two nursing care facilities from Centers Health Care affiliates for a combined $177.5M: Beth Abraham Center (612 Allerton Ave, Bronx, 448 beds) for $89M and a 314-bed Queens facility for $88.5M. The sale follows Centers Health Care's November 2024 settlement with the NY Attorney General over alleged financial fraud and resident neglect at four facilities, including these two.
stories.impact: Nursing home ownership transition in Bronx/Queens driven by regulatory distress does not directly impact multifamily. However, it signals operational challenges in senior-care real estate and regulatory tightening around healthcare operators in NYC; this may dampen investor appetite for mixed-use projects bundling assisted living/memory care with multifamily, and could increase equity cost and due-diligence burden for developers partnering with or financing senior-housing components.

stories.title: Schnitzer West Receives Approval for 456K-SF Office Tower in Bellevue
stories.excerpt: Seattle-based Schnitzer West has received city approvals for The Arcadian, a 19-story, 465,000-square-foot office tower in downtown Bellevue, WA. The project’s site plan and design review were approved Nov. 18. Located at 120 106th Ave., the development will replace an existing two-story, 44,400-square-foot commercial building formerly occupied by Rite Aid and a surface parking lot. Schnitzer West secured a ground lease for the 1.69-acre site from a local family investor in late 2021. The development will include 8,887 square feet of retail space, approximately 910 parking spaces across four subterranean levels and an 11,840-square-foot public plaza. Planned amenities include a rooftop coffee and wine bar, concierge services, a spa, a fitness club and a two-story rooftop gathering space. NBBJ designed the tower, which will feature a curved glass-and-metal exterior, brick detailing at street level and a stepped profile rising above a five-story podium. Sellen Construction is the general contractor. Schnitzer West anticipates completing the project in 2028, although the construction start date and the estimated development cost have not been disclosed. stories.summary: Schnitzer West received city approval for The Arcadian, a 465,000-sf, 19-story office tower in downtown Bellevue. Site plan and design review were approved November 18. The project replaces a former Rite Aid building and surface lot on a 1.69-acre ground lease. The tower will include 8,887 sf of retail, 910 parking spaces across four subterranean levels, and an 11,840-sf public plaza. Completion is targeted for 2028.
stories.impact: Major office tower approval in downtown Bellevue signals confidence in Seattle metro office fundamentals and mixed-use redevelopment pipeline; ground-lease model reduces developer capital intensity and de-risks equity. High parking count (910 spaces) reflects Bellevue auto dependence but may constrain near-term upside for office-to-residential conversion. Completion timing (2028) aligns with anticipated tech hiring normalization; successful office pre-leasing will validate regional employment demand and support adjacent or concurrent multifamily development in Bellevue downtown and Puget Sound corridor.
